back: Most important decisions are taken at the top of the organisation; gives control and consistency but is slow for local issues.
Decision-making authority is passed to lower levels; gives speed, local knowledge and motivation but may reduce consistency.
Directly produces or sells the goods or services (production, sales, distribution); line managers command subordinates.
Supports and advises the line (HR, finance, legal, IT); staff managers advise but do not normally command line managers.

front: Causes of line and staff conflict
back: Different objectives, staff advice not enforceable, lack of experience or consultation, competition for budget.
Centralise finance, branding and standards; decentralise local prices, service and staffing; depends on size, spread, skills, risk and need for consistency.
Personal relationships and groups among employees outside the official structure; has norms, leaders and the grapevine.
Pros: morale, quick information, teamwork. Cons: rumours, resistance to change, low output norms, exclusion.
Use informal leaders to explain change, listen to the grapevine, avoid breaking up helpful groups.
